open_items: IMF gateway metadata list_dataflows timeout (new shape, first ever on this endpoint): occurred cycle 756 only (2026-09-26T04:01:22Z), gateway metadata timed out after 60.0s (2 attempts); gateway data and both direct checks (metadata, json; IMF has no separate direct-data probe configured) stayed healthy. Resolved by cycle 757 (2026-09-26T06:01:22Z); see the 2026-09-26T06:43Z report entry. Live recheck of the direct dataflow listing at 06:43Z returned 200 in 0.6s (394KB payload), showing no provider-side slowness at recheck time. Resembles the recurring ESTAT list_dataflows 60s-deadline pattern (our own call deadline firing under load) but never previously seen on IMF; IMF's only prior flaps were the cycle 419 provider_down episode and the cycle 161 references:* 401 flap, both unrelated. Watch for a second occurrence; if it recurs, the standing ESTAT fix recommendation (raise deadline, stream listing, or cache parsed result in monitor/checks_gateway.py) likely applies to IMF too, but that is code-change scope, not actioned here.

Watch for a second occurrence.

ILO references:contentconstraint standalone 403 flap (new shape): first occurrence, cycle 703 (2026-09-21T18:01:22Z), classified broken (expected 200, observed 403). See the 2026-09-21T18:45Z report entry. Live recheck at 18:44Z already showed 200 again, byte-identical to references=none apart from volatile ID/timestamp fields, i.e. back to the documented ignored baseline. Endpoint status flipped healthy -> degraded for this one cycle; all five basic ILO checks and the other eleven contract assertions stayed healthy/ok throughout. Distinct from the cycle 226 blanket-403 episode (that one hit eight assertions plus both gateway basic checks together) and from the cycle 700 ignored -> ok heuristic flip (that one never left 200). Third overall broken/non-ignored reading on this assertion, after cycle 199 (same-cycle blip) and cycle 274 (500, resolved by cycle 275). Watch for a second standalone-403 occurrence; escalate for real if a future one persists past one cycle.

ILO references:contentconstraint verdict flipped ignored -> ok at cycle 700 (2026-09-21T12:01:22Z), observed status unchanged (200 -> 200); see the 2026-09-21T12:43Z report entry. Live recheck (message:ID and message:Prepared normalized out) showed the two probe responses byte-identical in substance, no ContentConstraint element in either, so the provider is still silently dropping the parameter; the flip was a 1-byte coincidence in ILO's volatile per-request ID/timestamp fields fooling the monitor's exact-byte-size ignored-detection heuristic. Also confirms a second instance of the changes-array gap already flagged for ABS on 2026-09-18: /api/contracts changes only diffs observed, not verdict, so this flip was invisible to every automated surface (changes array, history, status informational list) and was found only by manually diffing cycle 697-700 contract rows. BIS and IMF remain ignored on this same assertion, unaffected. Not actioned (code-change-scope fix to the heuristic and to the changes computation). No second occurrence of this specific ignored<->ok flip through cycle 703 (cycle 703's event was a genuine 200 -> 403 broken reading, not this heuristic coincidence). Treat any future ignored<->ok or ok<->broken flip on a byte-size-based assertion with the same suspicion.

ECB gateway_issue -> degraded episode, cycles 669-670 (2026-09-18T22:01:22Z, 2026-09-19T00:01:22Z): resolved by cycle 671, confirmed still healthy through cycle 703 (thirty-three consecutive clean cycles); see the 2026-09-19T06:42Z report entry closing out the 2026-09-19T00:43Z entry's open question. Remains the only ECB episode on record to span two consecutive cycles; it did not escalate further. No action needed; watch for a sixth distinct ECB failure shape.

ABS contract-only errors:missing_artefact 500 flap (new shape, bare): observed 500 (expected 404, verdict broken) at some cycle between 661 and 663, recovered by cycle 664 (2026-09-18T12:01:22Z); see the 2026-09-18T12:46Z report entry. Distinct from the 2026-08-13 cycle 234-235 flap, which hit dialect:sdmx3 and errors:missing_artefact together as 503, not this assertion alone as 500. Also surfaced a monitor tooling gap: /api/history's per-cycle status computation (monitor/main.py api_history) does not pass contract rows into derive_status, so a contract-only degraded cycle like this one never shows up in the history series even though /api/status would have shown it live; flagged as a code-change-scope fix, not actioned here. Watch for a second occurrence of this specific assertion/status combination.
